name: Drum and bass
blurb: Fast, chopped breakbeats over bass that moves at half the speed.

sounds.name: Chopped Amen break
sounds.why: Six seconds of drumming from a 1969 record, cut into slices and played back in a new order. Most of jungle and drum and bass is built on this one loop.

ingredients.name: The break, fitted to two bars
ingredients.adds: The whole recording, sped up or slowed down to last exactly two bars at this tempo.

ingredients.name: Cut it into eight
ingredients.adds: Eight equal slices, played in their original order.
ingredients.listenFor: It should sound the same. But each slice is now a note you can move.

ingredients.name: Play the slices out of order
ingredients.adds: Slices are repeated, skipped and doubled up.
ingredients.listenFor: The same drummer, playing a beat he never played.

ingredients.name: Clear out the bottom
ingredients.adds: Removes the lowest part of the break so the sub has that space alone.

knobs.label: cutoff
knobs.below: The break and the sub fight.

ingredients.name: Drive
ingredients.adds: Pushes the break so the quiet hits come up.

knobs.above: Crunch with no snare left in it.

pitfalls: Slicing into too many pieces loses the swing of the original drummer.

sounds.name: Two-step break
sounds.why: The cleaner alternative to a chopped break: the same kick-snare-kick-snare skeleton, programmed from single hits.

sounds.name: Reese bass
sounds.why: Two saws a hair out of tune, held on a long low note and filtered dark. As they drift against each other the bass slowly growls and churns.

ingredients.name: One sawtooth
ingredients.adds: A long, static, buzzy bass note.

ingredients.name: Two saws, slightly apart
ingredients.adds: A second saw plays the same note a little out of tune.
ingredients.listenFor: A slow beating inside the note. It moves though nothing is being played.

knobs.below: They line up: one saw again.

ingredients.name: Filter it dark
ingredients.adds: Only the low growl is left.

ingredients.name: Slow phaser
ingredients.adds: A filter that sweeps up and down through the sound on its own.

ingredients.name: Drive
ingredients.adds: Makes the beating between the saws louder and rougher.

pitfalls: A Reese takes up a lot of room. Play one long note where you would play eight short ones.

sounds.why: Long, deep notes at half the speed of the drums. The slow bass under the fast break is the whole trick.
Slow, lush chords floating over frantic drums. The pad moves at a quarter of the speed of everything else.
A short, bright chord with a long echo, dropped into the gaps of the break.
The crash and boom on the first beat of the drop, when the break and the bass come in together.
